open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict reuse and activation or rollback eligibility
open_points.kind: conditional validity without a model fact
open_points.text: “Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code that obtains neither [time nor chance]” conflicts with M08’s “recorded once and then reused, never computed again” and M09’s use of a new or reused admitted verdict, while K-02 says obtaining time or chance by another route “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
open_points.question: Does an admission verdict remain permanently reusable for activation and rollback when its implementation obtains time or chance through an undetected route, and, if not, what model fact or lifecycle change makes that verdict cease to authorize those actions?
options: The recorded verdict remains reusable regardless; the new condition limits only the behavioral guarantee that later executions repeat the trial results.
The verdict does not remain valid for such an implementation, requiring a fact that identifies the implementation as outside the repeatability promise and a defined invalidation or refusal lifecycle.
A later execution showing different behavior invalidates the verdict, even though no such transition is currently defined.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the recorded verdict reusable because the kernel does not detect alternate time or chance sources; treat the new sentence only as a limit on the guarantee of later behavior.

witness.initial: A contract version has a nonempty unchanged corpus. Implementation B obtains chance through an undetected route, happens to pass every admission trial, receives an admitted verdict, and is activated.
events: A real run executes B on the same relevant input and its chance-dependent branch produces a different result or fails; nobody captures the failure, so the corpus digest remains unchanged.
Another implementation is activated for the contract version.
The owner or an authoring agent asks to roll back to B.
outcomes: The kernel reuses B’s still-recorded admitted verdict over the current corpus and activates B, as M08 and M09 state.

The kernel treats B’s verdict as no longer holding under the new K-02 condition and refuses rollback or requires new qualification, although no verdict status, invalidation event, or qualifying fact is defined.
witness.observer: The owner or agent requesting rollback, and later callers whose runs pin B
